list: The official 55 trophies, as published by PlayStation and listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles, November 2026
sources: PlayStation official trophy descriptions, as listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles (November 2026)
In-game stats, mission and activity lists in Grand Theft Auto VI (PlayStation 5)

trophies.guide: The platinum unlocks the moment the other 54 trophies are yours, so treat this guide as the plan: play the story chapters in order, take every stranger strand as it appears, and do the activities alongside the story instead of leaving them for a dull cleanup phase. Save the big counters for last - 250 stunts, 50 challenges, the card sets and exploring every corner of Leonida - and finish with 100% completion. Expect a long haul of roughly 60 to 100 hours, and check the in-game stats screen often so a half-finished counter never surprises you at the end.
trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!

trophies.guide: Unmissable: this is the opening mission, Gone Fishing, and it unlocks as soon as you finish it. Follow the on-screen prompts through the mission's beats - driving, meeting the characters and the fishing itself - and do not rush the tutorial prompts, because this is where the game teaches its basic controls. There is nothing to prepare and nothing to fail permanently: if a beat goes wrong, the mission restarts from its last checkpoint and the trophy pops when the mission ends.
trophies.name: Just Like Paradise

trophies.guide: Story only, and unmissable: play through every mission of Chapter 1 in order and the trophy pops when the chapter closes. There is no side requirement and no count to track - just follow the main mission markers. Use Chapter 1 to learn the map and the driving, and pick up the early side activities (races, the shooting range) as they unlock, since the habits you build here pay off in the later chapters' longer missions.
trophies.name: Paradise Lost

trophies.guide: Story only, and unmissable: finish every mission in Chapter 2 and the trophy pops at the chapter's end. Chapter 2 is where the game's systems open up, so take the stranger strands and activities as they appear on the map rather than racing the main missions - the strands feed several other trophies, and doing them now keeps the endgame cleanup short. Keep a save before the chapter's final mission, as a habit, in case you want to replay its set-piece later.
trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money

trophies.guide: Story only, and unmissable: complete all of Chapter 3's missions and the trophy pops when the chapter ends. By now the map is mostly open, so this is a good chapter to clear the exploration and driving counters in between missions - discovering vehicles, visiting new areas of Leonida and trying the activities that have unlocked. Nothing in this chapter can be missed, but the missions get longer, so stock up on ammo and armour before the big set-pieces.
trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!

trophies.guide: Story only, and unmissable: finish Chapter 4 and the trophy pops. Before you push into the chapter's final missions, clear any stranger strands still open - several of them close or change once the story moves past this point, and their trophies are easier to earn while their characters are still giving you work. After Chapter 4, only the finale remains, so use the lull between missions to bank progress on the long counters: stunts, challenges and collectibles.
trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma

trophies.guide: Gold, story only and unmissable: complete the final mission and the trophy pops with the credits. Do your housekeeping before you start it - finish open stranger strands, collectibles and any missable trophies first, because the story's end is the point of no return for anything tied to a story moment. The final mission is long and combat-heavy, so go in with full armour, a stocked weapon wheel and a fast car. After the credits, free roam stays open for the cleanup trophies.
trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off

trophies.guide: Story mission trophy: complete the mission Breakfast Run and it pops at the mission's end. Like every named story mission, there is no extra objective to chase - finishing the mission is the whole requirement, and missions can be replayed from the pause menu if you ever need to. Play it when it appears in the story flow, follow the mission markers, and keep an eye on the mission's own twists: a failed attempt restarts from the checkpoint, not from the beginning of the mission.
trophies.name: Trust

trophies.guide: Story mission trophy: complete The Cartel Heist and it pops when the mission ends. Heist missions are the game's big set-pieces, so expect several phases - approach, execution and a getaway - and use the checkpoints between them. Bring your best weapons and a fast escape vehicle, and do not worry about style: the trophy only asks that the mission is completed, so a messy escape counts exactly the same as a clean one.
trophies.name: Break the Bank

trophies.guide: Story mission trophy: complete the mission Child's Play and it pops at the mission's end. Play it when it appears in the story flow; there is no side objective and no way to miss it, since the mission itself is the requirement. If a section gives you trouble, use the checkpoint restarts and take the mission's quieter approach where one is offered - rushing the loud option usually costs more time than it saves.
trophies.name: Family Matters

trophies.guide: Story mission trophy: complete the mission Headliners and it pops when the mission ends. Headliners is a story set-piece, so follow the mission markers through its phases and let the checkpoints carry you past any failed attempt - each retry starts from the last checkpoint, not the mission's start. There is no hidden objective, so play it straight and enjoy the scene; the trophy is for finishing, not for how stylishly you do it.
trophies.name: DWNFALL

trophies.guide: Story mission trophy: complete the mission VCIA Takedown and it pops at the mission's end. This one takes you into the airport, so expect tight corridors and close-quarters fighting mixed with open tarmac - a shotgun or SMG suits the interiors, and a rifle suits the runways. Use cover between the phases, keep moving during the takedown itself, and remember the mission can be replayed from the pause menu if you want to revisit it later.
trophies.name: Hi-Jacked

trophies.guide: Story mission trophy: complete Operation Savage Glory and it pops when the mission ends. This is a late-story military-style operation, so go in fully stocked: armour, rifle ammo and explosives, plus a sturdy vehicle for the approach. The mission runs in clear phases with checkpoints, so a failed push only costs you the current phase. Finish it and the story's last stretch opens up - do any remaining stranger strands before the finale.
trophies.name: Snow Storm

trophies.guide: Gold, and the last trophy most players earn: reach 100% completion, which the game tracks across story missions, stranger strands, collectibles, activities and challenges. Open the in-game stats or completion screen and work through whatever it still lists - that screen is the checklist, and this guide's other 54 trophies are most of the way there. The final few percent are usually a hidden collectible or an activity type you never tried, so chase the list, not your memory. Expect this to pop in the post-story cleanup, after 60 to 100 hours.
trophies.name: A Long Road

trophies.guide: Silver, and a pure counter: pull off 250 stunts of any kind - jumps, near misses, airtime, drifts and long wheelies all count, and the total accumulates across the whole game. The fastest way is to find a jump you can hit repeatedly, such as a ramp or a raised road edge, and loop it in free roam with a fast bike or car. You will earn a large share of the 250 naturally during the story; after the finale, grind the remainder in short sessions rather than one long sitting, and watch the in-game stats screen for the running total.
trophies.name: Cunning Stunts

trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try one of every activity type the game offers - races, fishing, the arcade, the shooting range, bowling, meditation, hunting, drone races and the other activities the map shows - and the trophy pops when the last type is sampled. Open the map and the activities list and work through the icons you have never touched; each one only needs a single attempt, not a win, so even a last-place race or a single round of bowling counts. Do this early, while you are learning the map, and the trophy comes almost for free.
trophies.name: Master of None

trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Silver, and the game's shooting exam: earn a gold medal in all 42 Shooting Range challenges. Each challenge scores accuracy, speed and target hits, so take it slow on your first run to learn the target pattern, then push for speed once you know where the targets appear. Use a weapon you are comfortable with, aim for the head and centre rings, and replay a challenge immediately while the layout is fresh in your memory - gold is a score threshold, not a one-shot test, so a missed run costs nothing but a retry.
trophies.name: The Shootist

trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at each of the locations the game lists, and the trophy pops when the last location is won. Drone races are flown through rings, so learn the course on a slow first lap, then cut corners through the rings on the timed run - smooth lines beat raw speed, and crashing costs more time than a cautious turn. Each location is a separate race, so you can win them in any order and in any session; the in-game race list shows which locations you still need.
trophies.name: Top Fun

trophies.guide: Win 20 different races - different events, not the same race 20 times. Work through the race list across the map: street races, off-road races, boat and air races if they are offered, and the activity races such as the drone events. Each race only needs one win, and a win counts even on the easiest setting, so pick a fast, stable vehicle you know, learn the first lap, and then push. The game tracks which races you have won, so check the race menu for the events still missing a win.
trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos

trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Missable, so do it when it is offered: beat Cal in a fishing challenge, which is a head-to-head fishing contest, not a story mission you can replay at will. When Cal's challenge appears, take it before the story moves on. In the contest itself, watch the line tension, reel steadily when the fish runs toward you and ease off when it pulls hard - snapping the line loses the catch. Land more or bigger fish than Cal within the challenge's limit and the trophy pops at the result screen.
trophies.missableWhy: Cal's fishing challenge may only be offered once - take it when it appears, before the story moves on.
trophies.name: Baited My Tackle

trophies.guide: Pick any arcade game in the game world, play it through to its end, and the trophy pops. Arcades are found in bars and entertainment spots around Leonida - walk up to a machine, start a game and see it through to the game-over or completion screen. Choose the shortest or simplest game on offer if you just want the trophy, and do not worry about a high score: completing the game is the requirement, not winning it. One finished arcade game is all it takes.
trophies.name: Stick Fiddler

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Missable, so do not leave Andy waiting: finish his strand by completing his final mission. Stranger strands unlock as you meet their characters around Leonida, and each one is a short chain of missions - follow Andy's marker whenever it appears, and finish the chain while his missions are still being offered. The trophy pops at the end of his last mission. If you are deep into the story, clear open strands now: a strand left unfinished can close once the story moves past it.
trophies.missableWhy: Stranger strands can close once the story moves on - finish Andy's chain while his missions are offered.
trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Missable, so do not leave Kenton waiting: finish his strand by completing his final mission. Kenton's missions appear as his marker on the map - take them as they come and follow the chain to its end, since a strand left unfinished can close once the story moves past it. The trophy pops when his final mission ends. Do the stranger strands alongside the story rather than saving them all for after the finale, and this one comes naturally.
trophies.missableWhy: Stranger strands can close once the story moves on - finish Kenton's chain while his missions are offered.
trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Missable, so do not leave Billy waiting: finish his strand by completing his final mission. Billy's missions appear as his marker on the map - take each one as it appears and follow the chain through to its last mission, since a strand left unfinished can close once the story moves past it. The trophy pops at the end of his final mission. Like the other stranger strands, this is best done during the story, not after it.
trophies.missableWhy: Stranger strands can close once the story moves on - finish Billy's chain while his missions are offered.
trophies.name: The Lone Rider

trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Silver, and the stranger-strand master trophy: complete 8 full mission strands for strangers across Leonida. Strangers appear as markers on the map as you explore and progress the story - each one is a short chain of missions ending in a finale, and this trophy counts finished chains, not single missions. Take every stranger marker as it appears, finish each chain before moving on, and keep a mental note of which strangers you have completed: Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy and Tyrone are five of them, and three more strangers are waiting elsewhere in the state.
trophies.missableWhy: A strand left unfinished can close once the story moves on - take every stranger marker as it appears.
trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Missable, so do not leave Randy waiting: finish his strand by completing his final mission. Randy's missions appear as his marker on the map - take them as they come and follow the chain to its end, since a strand left unfinished can close once the story moves past it. The trophy pops when his final mission ends. If you are working through the stranger strands in order, Randy's is one of the five named strands, and finishing it also counts toward the 8-strand trophy.
trophies.missableWhy: Stranger strands can close once the story moves on - finish Randy's chain while his missions are offered.
trophies.name: Supply & Demand

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Missable, so do not leave Tyrone waiting: finish his strand by completing his final mission. Tyrone's missions appear as his marker on the map - take each one as it appears and follow the chain through to its last mission, since a strand left unfinished can close once the story moves past it. The trophy pops at the end of his final mission. Finish the five named strangers - Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy and Tyrone - and you are most of the way to the 8-strand trophy as well.
trophies.missableWhy: Stranger strands can close once the story moves on - finish Tyrone's chain while his missions are offered.
trophies.name: Spin On This!

trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Find every meditation spot across Leonida and meditate at each one. Meditation spots are quiet, scenic places - hilltops, beaches, parks and viewpoints - and the game marks them once you are near or shows them in the activity list. Visit each spot, start the meditation and let it run to its end; the game tracks which spots you have used. Work through them region by region while you explore, and check the activity list for the spots still missing rather than wandering the map from memory.
trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude

trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Missable, so take Bret's hunt when it is offered: track down and hunt the one unique animal Bret asks for. Unique-animal hunts are one-off events - the animal appears in a specific area, and you need to track it, approach quietly and take a clean shot. Use the hunting tools the game gives you, follow the tracks and signs, and do not spook the animal into fleeing. If the hunt fails, retry it at once while Bret's request is still open; once the animal is down, the trophy pops.
trophies.missableWhy: A unique-animal hunt is a one-off event - take Bret's request when it appears and do not let it lapse.
trophies.name: Fair Game

trophies.guide: Silver, and a pure collectible hunt: find the cards hidden around Leonida and complete 3 full sets. Cards are tucked into interiors, alleys, rooftops and out-of-the-way corners - check behind counters, on shelves and in places the map does not signpost. The collection screen shows which cards you own and which sets are close to complete, so chase the sets with the fewest gaps first. There is no time limit and no missable window: after the story, sweep the map region by region and the third set will close.
trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck

trophies.guide: Silver, and a long exploration counter: use the WAiNK It action at locations all across Leonida until the count is complete. WAiNK It is an in-world interaction the game offers at marked spots - approach one, trigger it, and the location is logged. The fastest route is to work through the map region by region, hitting every WAiNK spot you pass while doing other activities, rather than hunting them in one dedicated sweep. The game tracks the count, so check the activity list for how many locations remain.
trophies.name: You WAiNKer!

trophies.guide: Complete 50 challenges - the game's small, varied objectives, from driving feats and combat goals to exploration and activity targets. Challenges are listed in the game's challenge menu, and each one shows its requirement and its progress, so pick the easy ones first: the short driving and combat challenges fall quickly, and the longer ones accumulate while you play normally. There is no time limit, so let the count grow across the story and then mop up the remainder from the challenge list in free roam after the finale.
trophies.name: One Last Thing

trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: Missable in practice, because it needs your partner beside you: build a 4-star wanted level while your partner is with you, then lose the heat together. Start a crime spree with your partner in the car - police attention climbs fast - then break line of sight, switch vehicles or hide until the wanted stars fade. The trophy pops when the 4-star level clears with your partner still with you. Do it during a story stretch where your partner is available; after the story, partner availability may be limited.
trophies.missableWhy: Needs your partner beside you - do it while a story stretch keeps your partner available.
trophies.name: Hot Together

trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: Missable in practice, because it needs your partner beside you: rob 3 shops in a row with your partner, keeping your wanted level the whole time. Pick three shops close together, rob the first, then drive straight to the next without letting the wanted level clear - the heat must stay on from the first robbery to the third. Keep the getaway car close, avoid killing anyone you do not have to, and do not stop to fight the police. The trophy pops after the third shop, while the wanted level is still active.
trophies.missableWhy: Needs your partner beside you, and the wanted level must survive all three robberies - do it while your partner is available.
trophies.name: Retail Therapy

trophies.guide: Drive, ride or simply approach 100 different vehicles and the game logs each new discovery. The fastest way is variety: steal or borrow every vehicle type you see - cars, bikes, trucks, boats and aircraft - and drive through the busy districts where traffic is thickest. The game tracks discoveries in the vehicle list, so check which classes are still missing and hunt those specifically. Most of the 100 come naturally during the story; after the finale, sweep the city streets and the countryside roads for the stragglers.
trophies.name: Whip It Good

trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Trigger Combat Focus once and take down 5 enemies before it ends. Set it up: find a fight with a group of enemies close together - a gang shootout or a police stand-off - and wait until at least five are in view before you trigger it. Use a fast, high-damage weapon, aim for headshots, and keep moving between targets instead of lingering on one. If the focus ends with fewer than five down, just try again: the trophy only needs one successful run, and the attempt itself costs nothing.
trophies.name: Gunslinger

trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Missable, so do it when the chance comes: make an unscheduled departure from Vice City International Airport - leave the airport in a way the schedule never planned. The cleanest reading of the trophy is to get to the airfield, take an aircraft or a vehicle, and leave VCIA without going through the normal departures: drive off the tarmac, take off from a runway, or otherwise exit the airport grounds by your own route. The trophy pops when you clear the airport's boundary in that unscheduled way.
trophies.missableWhy: Tied to a specific airport moment - make the unscheduled departure when you are at VCIA, rather than assuming you can repeat it later.
trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can

trophies.guide: Missable in practice, because it revolves around Rhino tanks: deal with the Rhinos - the game's main battle tanks - in the encounter where they appear. Tanks show up in the heavy set-pieces and in high wanted levels, so use cover, heavy weapons or explosives, and keep moving: a tank's cannon punishes standing still. If the encounter is a story set-piece, take it when it comes; if tanks appear at high wanted levels, build the heat in open ground where you can flank them. The trophy pops once the Rhinos are dealt with.
trophies.missableWhy: Rhinos appear in specific heavy encounters - deal with them when the encounter comes, not after it has passed.
trophies.name: Challenging Tank

trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store and get out without ever being detected. Go in quiet: enter the store calmly, avoid the cameras and the staff's line of sight, take the goods without smashing anything that raises the alarm, and leave before anyone notices. A suppressed weapon and patience help, but the real requirement is silence - no alarm, no witness, no police response. If you are spotted, leave at once and try again: the store can be robbed again, and the trophy only needs one clean run.
trophies.name: Sneakthief

trophies.guide: Silver, and a heist counter: rob 5 bank vaults and escape after each one. Each vault robbery has the same shape - get in, crack or force the vault, grab the cash, then lose the heat - so plan the escape before the robbery: a fast car parked close by, a route away from the police, and no lingering at the scene. You can space the five robberies across the game, and the count accumulates, so do one whenever you pass a bank and the heat is manageable, and the fifth escape pops the trophy.
trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal

trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Find an armored truck on the roads of Leonida, rob it, and escape. Armored trucks drive set routes through the city and countryside - spot one, block or ram it to a stop, deal with the guards, crack it open and take the cash. The robbery raises a wanted level, so have a getaway car ready and a route away from the police before you strike. The trophy pops once you have escaped cleanly; if the truck gets away or the police catch you, just find another one - they keep driving their routes.
trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play

trophies.guide: Visit every area of Leonida until the map is fully revealed. The game tracks exploration by area, so drive and fly through every region - the city districts, the beaches, the swamps, the countryside and the small towns - until the map shows no fog and no unvisited corner. Use a fast car for the roads and an aircraft for the far corners, and combine this with the other exploration counters (vehicles, meditation spots, WAiNK locations) so one sweep covers several trophies at once. The trophy pops when the last area is revealed.
trophies.name: The Goodtime State

trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Missable in practice, because some gang operations only appear while their gang is active in the story: rob one illegal operation belonging to each gang in Leonida. Illegal operations are gang-run spots on the map - stash houses, deals and smuggling runs - and each gang has its own. Hit one per gang, and be thorough: the game tracks which gangs you have hit, so check the list and chase the missing ones while their operations are still on the map. Do this during the story, when every gang is in play.
trophies.missableWhy: Some gang operations only appear while their gang is active in the story - hit every gang before the story moves on.
trophies.name: Pest Control

trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Go to Ocean Beach, find a bar or beach spot with a view of the ocean, and order a cocktail. The trophy is a quiet moment, not a challenge: walk the beachfront until you find the right spot, sit down with the view in front of you, and enjoy the drink. There is no timer and no failure state, so do it whenever you are passing Ocean Beach - it is a good palate cleanser between the story's louder missions, and it costs nothing but a few minutes of your time.
trophies.name: In The Beginning…

trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Missable, because it is tied to one showroom moment: smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style. When the showroom scene comes - a set-piece where you are inside a vehicle showroom - do not look for the polite exit: drive straight through the glass and out onto the street, the way the old games taught you. The trophy pops when you break out. If the moment is a story set-piece, take it when it comes; a showroom smashed later, in free roam, may not count the same way.
trophies.missableWhy: Tied to a specific showroom moment - smash out when the scene comes, rather than assuming a later free-roam attempt counts.
trophies.name: Capital Offense

trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Go to the Kolt & Associates bowling alley, play a game of bowling and follow through - finish the game, frame by frame, to its end. Bowling is a slow, calm activity: aim, set your power, and roll. You do not need a high score or a strike; the trophy is for playing the game through at this specific alley. It is a good break between missions, and it also counts as one of the activity types for the trophy that asks you to try everything once.
trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling

trophies.guide: Missable, because it is tied to a partnership story beat: build the partnership with mass appeal - a story moment where you and your partner make something the whole state notices. Play the story with your partner, take the partnership missions as they come, and the trophy pops at the beat itself; there is no separate objective to grind. If you rush the story without doing the partnership content, the moment can pass, so treat the partner missions as part of the main path, not an optional extra.
trophies.missableWhy: Tied to a partnership story beat - play the partner missions as they come, or the moment can pass.
trophies.name: Personal Best

trophies.guide: Missable in the small, because it counts the choices you make: keep making choices across the game - dialogue choices, mission approaches, who you help and who you cross - and the count accumulates toward the trophy. The description's count is tracked by the game, so the honest method is simply to play the story fully and choose actively instead of always taking the default path. Some choices only appear once, in a single mission, so do not skip dialogue or rush past a decision point: a choice you never see cannot be counted.
trophies.missableWhy: Some choices appear only once, inside a single mission - choose actively and do not skip decision points.
trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder

trophies.guide: Missable in the small, because it is about retrying: fail something, then succeed on the second try. The trophy's shape is a second attempt that works - a mission, a challenge or an activity you fail once and then clear on the immediate retry. If you are stuck on a mission or a challenge, do not restart from a save: retry from the failure screen and finish it on the next attempt, and the trophy pops. It is one of those trophies that comes naturally if you play honestly and do not reload old saves to erase failures.
trophies.missableWhy: Needs a genuine failed attempt followed by a successful retry - do not reload old saves to erase failures.
trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess

trophies.guide: Missable, because it is a one-off world event: witness something strange in Leonida - one of the game's odd, unscripted moments that happens in a particular place at a particular time. Explore widely and slowly: drive the back roads at night, walk the strange corners of the map, and stop when something looks out of place. The event is easy to rush past, so if you hear or see something odd, stay and watch it play out. The trophy pops when the strange thing happens in front of you.
trophies.missableWhy: A one-off world event, easy to rush past - explore slowly and stay to watch anything strange.
trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There

trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Knock someone down with a melee drive-by: attack with a melee weapon from a moving vehicle and bowl your target over. The setup is simple - a slow-moving car or bike, a melee weapon in hand, and a target close to the road - and the execution is a drive-by swing as you pass. Pedestrians on a quiet street are the easiest targets, but be ready for the wanted level that follows: hit, keep driving, and let the heat fade. One clean melee drive-by knockdown pops the trophy.
trophies.name: Ten Pin

trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Earn $250,000 by laundering Marked Bills through your contacts. Marked Bills are the dirty money you pick up from robberies and heists - they cannot be spent as-is, so take them to your contacts and launder them into clean cash. The total accumulates, so keep robbing and keep laundering: bank vaults, armored trucks and shop robberies all produce Marked Bills. Check your contacts list for who will launder, and do it regularly - a big pile of dirty money is worth nothing until it is cleaned.
trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar

trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all the shops of Leonida - clothes, weapons, car parts, food, anything the shops sell. The total accumulates across every purchase, so there is no need to save up and spend it at once: just buy what you need as you play, and the trophy will pop in the natural course of a long playthrough. If you are close to the total late in the game, top it up with big-ticket items - a vehicle upgrade or a full wardrobe - and check the stats screen for the running total.
trophies.name: Treat Yo Self

trophies.guide: Buy every garage property the game offers. Garages appear on the map and in the property listings as you progress - each one costs money, so save up and buy them as they unlock rather than spending everything on cars first. A garage is both storage and a trophy: owning them all pops this trophy, and the extra storage makes the vehicle-collecting trophies easier. Check the property list for the garages still unowned, and buy the last one when you can afford it.
trophies.name: Little Boxes

trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app. Find a vehicle, take it, and register it through the app on your in-game phone - each registration counts, and different vehicles all count toward the ten. The easiest route is to grab the varied traffic you see on the streets: cars, bikes and the odd truck, registering each one as you go. The app shows how many you have registered, so check it when you are unsure how many are left, and the tenth registration pops the trophy.
